Commentary.Commentary: A solid response from the Indians after being pummeled in the beginning by Liton Das. Once again, it was Jadhav who managed to find the breakthrough when the rest were struggling. It was him who broke that opening stand and then picked the prized scalp of Mushfiqur Rahim, which led to the eventual Bangladeshi collapse. Three run outs didn't help their cause either. The rest joined in, with Kuldeep bagging 3 and Chahal and Bumrah having a wicket apiece. 223 is a target which India will fancy, but a couple of early wickets on this already slow surface about to slow down more could make things interesting. Let's see what happens on the other side of the break.

A good comeback from the Men in Blue after getting battered in the early part of the innings. Mainly, in the death overs, where Bumrah and Bhuvi were right on the money, a complete contrast to how they performed in Powerplay 1. Bangladesh will be quite disappointed with what they have on the board, especially after the rollicking century opening stand between Das and Mehidy. But after that, a major collapse followed. Only 3 batsmen in total went on to get double figures, with one of them being Liton, who grabbed his maiden ODI ton. That says a lot about both their batting and the Indian bowling.

OUT! GONE! This is some exceptional death bowling from Jasprit Bumrah. As he has been in this last spell, he comes steaming in and fires a yorker on the stumps. Rubel Hossain makes room, looks to dig it out but it's too good for him. His stumps are rattled and that brings about an end to the innings. BANGLADESH ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 222!
Full and arrowed around leg, catches Rubel low on the pads.
Rubel Hossain is the last batsman in for Bangladesh.

OUT! He is. Superb run out from the Indians, particularly MS Dhoni. He shows good awareness here. Sarkar awkwardly slaps the pull through mid on. Takes one, and then calls for the second. Rayudu charges to the ball from the deep and fires it at the striker's end. Dhoni sees this, runs towards the stumps, collects the ball with the momentum and takes the bails off. He wasn't sure, but it's taken upstairs. Replays roll in and show that Soumya is just short.
Run out appeal! Is he gone? Soumya Sarkar the man in question.
Big swing and a big miss. Back of a length on middle and leg, Mustafizur goes for the big heave but connects only with thin air.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.

Switches to 'round the wicket, it's angling in on leg. It keeps going down with the angle and catches Rahman on the pads as he looks to work it across the line. An appeal goes up, but it's turned down, probably missing leg or clipping at best.
Shaping away from around off, dabbed square towards point for a single.
Wide! Too far outside off, across the tramline and a wide is signalled.
Right on the money again. Wow. This is superb bowling. Yorker around leg. Sarkar barely manages to dig it out.

FOUR! Not a bad bat at all, just some good fortune on Sarkar's end. Yorker around leg, Soumya somehow gets some bat on it and it runs down to fine leg off the inner half. The fielder at the rope tries to stop it with a dive, but can't.
Full toss on off, played to point. A superb over from Bumrah, a wicket and 3 runs off it. 1 run came off a wide.

Another run out chance, but this one goes abegging. Mustafizur plays it towards point and takes off. Is sent back, similar to the previous delivery, and Pandey has a shy at the striker's end. Misses but it's not over. Bhuvi who is backing up at short mid-wicket, collects and seeing Sarkar out of his crease too, looks to score a direct hit at the bowler's end but misses as well. All happening here. Good to see the players smiling.
Mustafizur Rahman is next in.

OUT! Run out! Nazmul Islam is out of here. This is good bowling from Bumrah. He spears in another yorker around leg, hits the batsman low on the pads and a loud appeal goes up which is turned down. During all this, Islam takes off as the ball rolls to point but his partner Sarkar doesn't. Nazmul has to track back after coming more than halfway down the track but by this time he's gone for all money. Manish Pandey (sub) has so much time that he runs to the stumps and takes the bails off with no trouble.
Full outside off, pushed through the cover area for one.
An accurate yorker, on leg stump, Sarkar looks to stay leg side and drill it through the off side, but instead gets an inside edge back onto his pads.
Slanting across on a full length, outside off, driven a bit square just wide of sweeper cover. Single to the total.
Wide! Down the leg side, Islam looks to flick but misses. Wide signalled.
Full in length on leg stump, clipped neatly through the leg side, more specifically through square leg, for a brace.

Beautiful. A pinpoint yorker on leg, curling back in, Sarkar can't do anything about it as the ball goes off his boot and lobs behind. Dhoni moves to his left and collects, stopping the batsmen from taking the single.
Switches to around the wicket and lands it outside off on a length. It holds its line as Islam cuts it behind point. Another two on offer but the batsmen take one.
Fraction straight in line, easy peasy for Islam to work it off his pads through square leg for a couple of runs.

A little much width offered outside off, Nazmul drives it through the big gap in the covers. The sweeper has to cover some decent ground to his left, which allows the batsmen to come back for the second.
Hits that full length again, almost a yorker on off, drilled down to long off by Soumya for a run.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar also returns.
Nazmul Islam has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good running. Sarkar pats it down in front of point and both batsmen take off. Rush across and complete the run with ease.
Slanting across on a good length, around off, Soumya goes back and pushes it away on the off side beside the track.
Another yorker, on leg stump, Islam looks to work it away but it goes off his boot to the square leg region. A leg bye is taken.
On the fuller side of things again, around off, Islam blocks it with the full face of the bat.
Wastes no time as he fires in the yorker, on the stumps, Sarkar somehow manages to dig it out off the inside edge onto his pads. It rolls on the off side and a single is taken.
Jasprit Bumrah is back to have a go with the ball.
Turning in sharply from around the wicket, outside off, Islam goes deep inside the crease and blocks it down on the off side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A lot of air outside off, turning back in, drilled through the covers for one run.
Full toss on leg, eased down to long on. One run to the total.
Spinning in on leg stump, Islam looks to flick but it goes off the pads.
Flat, short and spinning in on off, Soumya offers a firm punch down the ground to long on for a single.
On a flatter trajectory, kept out watchfully.
Nazmul Islam walks into the middle next.

OUT! Kuldeep has bamboozled Mortaza completely to get a 3-fer! Classic deception to get rid of the Bangladesh skipper. He spots Mortaza using his feet and hence, bowls a googly on a flatter trajectory and it is outside off as well. It spins a long way away as Mashrafe swings wildly across the line probably not picking the wrong one. He ends up missing it completely. Dhoni behind does the rest, he will affect such stumpings in his sleep too. Another achievement regarding which MS will be proud of as this is his 800th dismissal in international cricket. India keep on chipping away at the wickets. Can they bowl out Bangladesh before their allotted quota of overs?
Good bowling from Kuldeep! He spots Mortaza making room and bowls a googly outside off. Mashrafe swings through the line but misses.
Tossed up ball, defended nicely off the front foot.
SIX! In the arc, out of the park! Slower through the air around off, Mortaza kneels on one knee and nails the slog sweep over mid-wicket. Deep into the stand she goes. Wonderful hit.
Tossed up on middle and off, Mortaza makes room and slaps it hard but finds the point fielder.
Mortaza skips down the track and smacks it to wide long off for a single.
Flights it up there around off, pushed away gently with soft hands.
Stifled shout, but the impact is outside leg. Chahal with the quicker one on leg, it keeps going down with the angle, Mortaza goes back to play at it but is caught on the pads.
Slow through the air, landed on a driveable length, Mortaza plants his front foot forward and sees it out.
Goes with the spin and wrists it down to long on for a single.
Tossed up leg break on middle and leg, blocked from the front foot.
Mashrafe Mortaza is the next batsman in. Also, Yuzvendra Chahal to bowl again.

OUT! Superb work from MS Dhoni! Kuldeep bowls the wrong 'un around off, Das doesn't pick it up as he comes forward to block. Is beaten past the outside edge and his back leg drags out of the crease. Now, seeing this, and given how quick Dhoni is with the gloves, is a dangerous thing. MS whips the bails off and it's taken upstairs. Though, the Indian keeper signals it took him an extra second than usual due to the extra bounce. Anyway, the TV umpire has several looks at it. From different angles the foot seems to be behind the line, but from the stump cam it looks like the foot is on the line. But, it's signalled out eventually. Strange, as when one looks at it so many times, the benefit of the doubt is usually given to the batsman. Just something out of the ordinary from the usual norm. In any case, a wonderful knock from Liton Das comes to an end. Maybe just at the wrong time. Also, with this, Dhoni becomes the keeper with the most stumpings in Asia Cup, overtaking Kumar Sangakkara.
Lightning quick hands from Dhoni and a referral for a stumping has gone upstairs. Touch and go from the looks of it. Let's see...
Served on leg, spinning away towards off, Liton is down to sweep but misses and wears it on the body.
Deft from Liton. It's well outside off, he plays this late again past short third man. Chahal once more chases it down and two runs are taken.
FOUR! Loopy and right in the slot, Das clears his front leg and hammers it straight over the bowler's head. Beats the long on and finds the fence.
Short on the stumps, pulled with a little swivel to deep mid-wicket for a double.
Spinning in from outside off, on a shorter length, Das waits for it, uses the pace and runs it down towards third man. Chahal from inside the circle hares after it and keeps the batsmen down to two.
Powerplay 3 has been signalled. A maximum of 5 fielders will be allowed outside the ring till the end of the innings. Also, Kuldeep Yadav is back into the attack.
Played to the point region by the batsman. 10 runs have come from this.
Moves inside the line with a step across the stumps and turns it through backward square leg for a single.
The left-hander does the same. Punches it square through point and gets to the other end.
Short, flat and on off, Liton backs away to this and cuts it square through the off side for a single.
Drives it down the ground towards long on for a single.
SIX! What a shot! Floated up, Sarkar walks down the track and swings across the line. Makes sweet connection on the slog and clears the mid-wicket rope with ease. A boundary after 63 balls.
Cut late down to third man and a single is taken.
Works it to backward point. No run taken on this occasion.
Well outside off, on a good length, dabbed behind point with an open face for a single.
Fuller in length outside off, driven crisply but straight to the man at extra cover.
Another inside edge, on the pads this time. Bumrah angles it in on a length on off, Liton just about survives again.
Bumrah angles this on a back of a length on off, Das looks to force it through the off side but gets a bottom edge right beside him. Could have just as easily dragged it back on.
Full delivery drifting in from around off, eased away to the cover area. Dot ball to end the over.
Liton moves across his sticks to this fuller ball on off and works it behind square on the leg side for one.
Short again, cut fiercely but can't pierce the gap. Straight to point.
Short and flat close to off, punched away on the off side.
Darts it full and flat outside off, Das reaches out to play at it but misses.
Full and straight from Kedar, Liton plays it back to him.
Angling in on middle and leg, easy enough for Sarkar to pick it off his pads and work it square through the leg side for a brace.
Sarkar has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Beaten again! Bumrah is tempting Sarkar by giving him that width outside off. It's full in length, so the southpaw looks to play the booming drive through the cover region for nothing.
Behind a good length, close to off, Sarkar with one more defensive shot.
Bumrah offers room outside off, a length ball. Sarkar has a feel for it but gets beaten.
From around the wicket, it's coming in on a bit of a fuller length, Soumya defends it safely.
Jasprit Bumrah back on.
Another quick single. Soumya pats this down and both batsmen hurry through across.
Cuts this short ball late down towards third man for a couple of runs.
Outside off, placed square to point.

Not out! Sarkar works it away towards backward square leg and takes off. Sarkar takes off, then turns back and the throw is fired in at Dhoni. He takes the bails off but doesn't have the ball in his hands as he does so. So Sarkar is safe and lucky too, because if Dhoni had collected it cleanly, he would have been gone.
A run out appeal is taken upstairs. India don't look too confident though.
Fullish in length, around off, another block.
Drifting in from around off, from around the wicket, Sarkar is well forward in defense.

Drinks are on the field. India have come back into this game well. From 120/0, Bangladesh slipped to 151/5. The game, however, isn't in anyone's favour for the time being at least. This next phase of play could determine which way the tide turns. Crucial juncture for both sides.
Quite full and very loopy outside off, Das comes forward, gets low and drives it right at the cover fielder.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
Turning in on middle and leg, full in length, swept down to fine leg for a single.
Nicely done from the Indian skipper. Sarkar wrists this away towards short mid-wicket where Rohit dives to his right and keeps the batsmen to just the one.
On the fuller side of things, turning away, blocked with a defensive blade in response.
Extremely full on middle and off, so full that the ball has no space to turn. Sarkar flicks it to short mid-wicket.
Full on the stumps, quicker in pace, played to mid on for a run.
Uses the depth of the crease to go deep inside and defends.
Down the ground again, towards long off once more, and another single to the total.
Comes half-forward and drives it to long off for a single.
Sliding in on middle and off from around the wicket, blocked from inside the crease.
Wide! Darted too far outside off, across the tramline, Soumya lets it be. Wide called.
Flatter and quicker in line of the stumps, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for one.
Some issue out in the middle. The batsman has a problem with the tape Jadhav has on his right palm. He's asked to take it off by the officials after a discussion with all parties involved.
Kedar Jadhav returns.

Ooh.. Close. Wasn't that far away. Kuldeep lands it on middle and it spins away. Sarkar is on the back foot to defend but it goes past the outside edge and raps him on the thigh pad. The impact is outside off though.
Beaten! Superb. Flighted outside off, spinning away a touch, Sarkar is forward to push it away but fails to make connection.
Landed short and on the stumps, pulled away down towards fine leg for one.
Some good drift on this from Kuldeep, on middle and off, blocked from deep inside the crease.
Soumya Sarkar to bat next.

OUT! That's a good catch from Bumrah out in the deep. Bangladesh are suffering a bit of a collapse here. Tossed up around off, spinning in, it's quite slow through the air and Mahmudullah as a result doesn't connect well with the slog sweep. Skies it towards deep mid-wicket where Jasprit moves to his right and gobbles it up well, with a little slide at the end. The all-rounder could have avoided this shot as his side had lost wickets in a heap. The big boundaries in Dubai are proving fatal for Bangladesh.
The googly on middle and leg, Liton nudges it to square leg and both batsmen scamper through for the run.
Looks to tap this behind point but the placement isn't perfect. Finds the fielder. Jadeja there misfields, but doesn't concede a run.
Mahmudullah has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Keeps it tight. A length ball on off, blocked with bat and pad kept close together.
Waits for the ball to come, opens the face and runs it down to third man for a single.
Good effort from Jaddu. Das plays a punchy-drive towards cover. It would have gone for runs but Jadeja dived full stretch to his left and stopped it.
Length delivery just outside off, cut hard but straight to point.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar is brought back into the attack. He had a torrid first spell, can he make amends now?
Rocks back to this short ball and pulls it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
A lot of air from Kuldeep, on the stumps, Mahmudullah is on the front foot to block it out.
Spinning away from around off, played to point for no run.
Full on off, defended right under his eyes.
Positions himself right behind the line and blocks it out.
Kuldeep Yadav is back.
Leans ahead and knocks it through to long off for a single.
Floated delivery around off, Mahmudullah meets it with a defensive bat in response.
Another one blocked. It's straight in line, kept out safely.
Short and flat on the stumps, pulled along the carpet through to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Some air on this as it's landed full, blocked without any problem.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Jadeja is back.
Full ball on middle, driven down to mid on.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Maiden ODI ton for Das! He was dropped twice but he has done really well to capitalize on it. Fullish ball on middle, knocked down to long on for a run. He lifts his helmet and soaks in all the applause. He however needs to carry on as his side is in a precarious situation.
FOUR! Shot! Tossed up ball on off, Das slog sweeps it over backward square leg for a boundary. Moves to 99 with that.
Slower through the air, tucked off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Mahmudullah is the new man in.

OUT! Take a bow, Jadeja! He is one of the best fielders in the world if not the best. Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, Das drives it hard towards extra cover. Ravindra moves to his left in a flash and dives full length to stop the ball. Liton is guilty of ball watching as Mithun hares towards him. Jadeja first shapes to aim at the keeper's end but spots that both the batsmen are at the same end and hence, has the presence of mind to throw it back to Chahal who takes the bails off. Meanwhile, Liton got back in his crease first so Mohammad has to depart. Bangladesh have lost four wickets in a jiffy. Jubilation for the Men in Blue while agony for the Bangla Tigers.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Floated in line of the stumps, eased off the front foot towards mid on.
Driven towards the mid off region. One run added to the total.
Floated a bit wider outside off, Mithun goes for a booming drive but gets an outside edge past the vacant slip region towards short third man.
Tossed up ball, flicked against the spin to mid-wicket.
Tossed up on middle, driven down to long on for a run. Another productive over for India.
Mohammad Mithun is the next batsman in.

OUT! This is a big, big breakthrough for India! It is Jadhav again who has spun his web around the opposition. Coming back to the ball, it is short around off and is asking to be hit. Rahim camps back and goes for the big pull across the line but the only mistake he makes is that he picks out the deep mid-wicket fielder to perfection. Bumrah doesn't need to move an inch and takes it with ease. A disappointed Mushfiqur indicates to his partner that the ball hit his bat a bit higher than he would have liked. The ground in Dubai is pretty big and you need to give it your all if you want to clear the boundaries. Back at his home, that would have been a biggie. The pick of the batsmen for the Bangla Tigers fails this time. Bangladesh are losing their way.
On a flatter trajectory, cut away against the spin to point.
Shorter in length, punched out off the back foot.
Spinning into Das who leans ahead and knocks it through mid on for a single.
Too full and straight, milked down with ease to long on for a run.
Floated delivery in line of the stumps, Liton leans ahead and blocks it down the track. Another tidy over from Chahal, only two from it.
Das goes for the cut to the quicker one but it is too close to cut. Ends up getting a bottom edge past the keeper.
Flighted ball in line of the stumps, Liton prods forward in defense.
Quicker through the air on a fullish length outside off, slog swept towards deep mid-wicket. Some aggressive running between the wickets allows the batsmen to come back for the second run.
Chahal drags his length back and Liton hangs back to stonewall it.
The googly on middle, Das clears his front leg and keeps it at bay.
FOUR! Well played! Shorter in length, ample time for Rahim to rock back and cut it through covers for a rocketing boundary. Gets off the mark too.
Slower through the air and it's around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Short and wide, it has been cut away but it is straight to the point fielder.
On a flatter trajectory, doesn't spin much. Rahim camps back and dead-bats it.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Slower through the air, kept out watchfully.
Floated outside off, eased to point.
The man who is in great form, Mushfiqur Rahim, comes out to bat.

OUT! The impact is umpire's call and Kayes has to make the long walk back! Bangladesh don't lose the review but they lose another wicket in quick succession. Tossed up generously around off, Kayes leans ahead and tries to smother the spin but is hit flush on the pads. The Indians go up in unison and the umpire has no hesitation in raising his finger. Imrul walks gingerly to his partner and after some thought, challenges the decision. Time for the replays. The question is whether it brushes his front pad before hitting the back pad and that is where impact might come into question. Yes, it did kiss it. Hawk Eye rolls in and the impact is umpire's call, before going on to crash into the stumps. A great phase of play for India.
Seems like India have got another one. Kayes has been trapped in front of the stumps. Looks dead to the naked eye. The impact is the only thing which can save him.
Tossed up ball in line of the stumps, tucked with a closed bat face to mid-wicket.
Fuller in length, driven down towards mid on.
Spinning into Kayes who clips it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Nicely done! Short and width on offer, cut away past backward point for a brace. Moves to the nineties with that. Unlike Mehidy, he waited for the ball and placed it nicely.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Kayes clears his front leg and beats the diving fielder at extra cover with his drive. Takes a run and is off the mark.
Slower through the air and floated above the eye-line of the batsman. It has been driven towards covers.
On a flatter trajectory this time, punched out off the back foot to the off side.
Loopy delivery around off, Das leans ahead and drives it down to long off for a single.
Quicker through the air on middle and leg, tucked off the back foot to the leg side.
Wide! Was there a nick? The umpire doesn't think so. There was a sound alright. Down the leg side, Kayes looks to flick but seems to have missed it. It has been wided by the umpire.
Tossed up a bit wider outside off, Liton reaches to the pitch of the ball and caresses it to sweeper cover to change strike.
Loopy full ball on off, knocked down to long on for a run.
Slower through the air and the wrong one, Kayes comes forward and defends it tentatively.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Tossed up outside off, tapped off the front foot towards point.
Yuzvendra Chahal is back.
Darted in on middle and leg, tucked towards mid-wicket. A wicket and 4 from the over.
Imrul Kayes comes in to bat. He has been promoted up the order.

OUT! The man with the golden arm has struck gold for India! Jadhav bowls a tossed up ball around off and there is no pace on it. Mehidy rocks back and tries to cut it away but mistimes it completely. Rayudu at cover-point stands his ground and pouches it safely. Brilliant captaincy from Rohit Sharma. He deliberately didn't keep anyone out in the deep and Mehidy fell into the trap. A superb opening stand has been cut short, 120 to be precise. Is this the opening India needed?
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Shoddy from India! Tossed up ball on middle, Mehidy works it towards mid-wicket and sets off for a run. Jadeja picks up the ball but his throw is way off target at the bowler's end. The batsmen take an extra run.
Quick and flat on middle and leg, turned around the corner to rotate strike.
Starts off with a half-tracker on off, doesn't rise because of his low-arm action. Pulled away hard to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Kedar Jadhav comes on for a bowl. India need a wicket. Can he be the man for them?
Played square to point once more. End of the over.
Short and wide, cut hard straight to backward point.

FOUR! Another sweep behind square on the leg side and another boundary. Rohit Sharma looks a frustrated man. Das is down again and places it through backward square leg for the second one of the over.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Backs away to this shorter one outside off and dabs it towards short third man.
FOUR! Darted in on middle and off, not much turn on this. Liton Das leans forward and across and sweeps it through backward square leg for a boundary.
A good over for Bangladesh. 6 from it. It ends with Mehidy staying right behind the line and meeting it with the full face of the bat.
Comes forward, reaches out to it and pushes it to long off. One run to the total.
Hasan works it away on the leg side too and changes ends.
Rotating the strike well here. Liton just turns it away in front of square on the leg side and crosses over.
Spinning away from around off, cut down late towards third man for two more.
A little too full outside off, the ball doesn't even turn as Hasan drives it through to sweeper cover for a run.

Drinks break. A totally unexpected start from Bangladesh. Everyone thought early wickets would come, but the opening pair of Mehidy and Liton has powered past the three-figure mark, with the latter taking the charge and scoring a fifty. The Indian bowlers look clueless, and in desperate need of a wicket. They need one quickly too.
Fuller and quicker on off, blocked safely from the front foot.

FOUR! Plays this very late. Nicely done. Seeing the ball landing short, Das is on the back foot in a flash and cuts it late down to third man for a boundary. The 100-run stand comes up for Bangladesh. This is their second century stand for the opening wicket against the Indians in ODIs. When the first one happened, the Tigers had won that encounter.
Drifting in on middle and leg, driven to mid on.
Similar ball, probably a bit quicker through the air, driven to the cover region again.
Full outside off, pushed to covers.
Closes the face to flick it against the spin. Into the leg side and that's a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. End of the over.
Hangs back and keeps it out off the back foot with soft hands.

Safe! Not all that close after all. Mehidy works it just wide of short fine leg and both batsmen take off. Dhawan moves to his right, picks it up and fires it to the keeper who deflects it onto the stumps as Das slides his bat in. It's taken upstairs and replays show that Liton is well in. Dhoni's body language didn't show much confidence either, so that probably was a telling sign.
A run out chance! This could be touch and go. Dhawan's throw has been deflected onto the stumps by Dhoni. Over to the third umpire now...
Floated up outside off, pushed straight to the man at cover.
Loopy full toss outside off, driven to long off for a single.

Close one! Kuldeep loops this up and bowls the googly around leg, Das closes the face early to flick and it goes off the leading edge through the vacant slip position. Short third man chases it down and keeps the batsmen to two.
Driven through the vacant mid off region, to the fielder in the deep, for one run.

Good save from Rayudu out in the deep, saved a certain boundary. Liton kneels down and sweeps it through mid-wicket. Ambati moves to his left and slides, keeping it just inside the rope. Two runs added to the total.
Finds the cover fielder with a tame drive from the front foot.
FOUR! Nicely played. Short ball on the stumps, Das rocks onto the back foot in a jiffy and pulls it with a lot of power over mid-wicket for a boundary.
A big appeal but it's turned down. Too far down the track maybe. Liton gives the charge and looks to go big over the leg side but is rapped on the pads. The umpire shuts it down quickly.
Sliding in with the arm on off stump, a straight blade is offered in response.
On the back foot this time, blocked once more.
Seeing the flight Mehidy gets low early and nicely paddles it fine down the leg side. Gets it wide of short fine leg and comes back for the second.
Full and attacking the stumps, blocked with the full face of the bat from the front foot.
Worked away on the leg side. Dot ball.
FOUR! Landed full and wide, Mehidy shifts his weight on the front foot and slices it wide of the point fielder. The dive is put in but to no avail. It races away to the fence for a boundary.
Draws the batsman forward by tossing it up outside off, Das drives it to long off by reaching out to it. Single taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Makes connection on the cut but finds the man at point.
Beaten! Arm ball sliding in, a little too close to cut but Mehidy still goes for it. Gets beaten and Jadeja appeals, thinking there might be a feather, but opts out of it quickly.
Presents a firm defensive punch as he plays it towards the cover fielder again.
Quicker through the air, outside off, pushed off the front foot to cover.
Quite full outside off, eased back down the ground to wide long off. The batsmen change ends.
Turns it away with the spin into the empty mid-wicket area. One run to the total.
Spinning in from outside off, Hasan is forward as he pats it square on the off side. Calls for the run and both respond. Quick single results.
Loopy and full on the stumps, places this wide of mid off at the edge of the circle for a run.
Positions himself behind the line and defends with ease.
Short ball turning in on middle and leg, pulled away in front of square leg along the turf for a single.
Flighted delivery full in length on off, drilled back in the bowler's direction.
Mehidy goes down the ground too, to long off and keeps strike.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Knocks it down the ground to long off for one.

DROPPED! Das gets a second reprieve in this innings. This should have been taken though. Jadeja floats this up on off, Liton is down on one knee to play the big slog sweep but gets a top edge as he can't make proper connection. It lobs up towards mid-wicket where Chahal tracks back, gets his hands to it but can't hold on. Two runs taken. Nobody is happy with that. Chahal might have suffered a concussion with that, as he fell on the back of his head after he fluffed the chance. Surprisingly, nobody's out to look at him.
Das is forward to this fuller length ball and keeps it out.

FOUR! Maiden ODI fifty for Liton Das! What a time to bring it up too and in some style as well. Welcomes Jadeja with a boundary. Too full outside off, drilled through the covers for a rocketing boundary. With the start he's got, he'll want to make it count now.
Ravindra Jadeja is on now.
Prods forward and blocks it out with the full face of the bat.
Play and a miss! Should have dispatched, really. A lot of air and too full outside off, Mehidy comes forward to play the cover drive but fails to make any kind of connection.
Turning in from a shorter length, flicked down in front of mid-wicket.
Tossed up again, outside off, finds the cover fielder again with the drive.
Looped up outside off, driven straight to the man at cover.
Goes back to the ball spinning in and works it away into the leg side for a single.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled! Maximum of four fielders are now allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over. Meanwhile, Kuldeep Yadav comes into the attack.
Mehidy has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. A brilliant Powerplay 1 for Bangladesh. They have a nice foundation now.

A loud shout for an LBW but it falls on deaf ears! On a length on middle and leg, straightening a touch. Hasan shuffles across and tries to work it around but is hit high on the pads. An appeal ensues but the umpire stays put. India do not take the review. Replay shows that it would have clipped the top of the stumps and hence, no harm done.
Fullish ball around off this time, tapped off the front foot towards cover-point.
Too straight from Kumar, he has failed to hit the tight off stump corridor today. It has been flicked away nicely towards mid-wicket.
Tentative! Had he missed there, he was a clear candidate for LBW. Full length ball, shaping in late. Liton comes half-forward and gets it off the inner half towards square leg. A run taken.
On a good length around off, seaming in. Liton covers the line well and answers it with a straight bat.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar is back on.
Short of a length ball, angling in from outside off. Das stays back and taps it towards third man for a run. 6 from this over. The pacers have looked toothless so far.
On a length, angling in, Liton drives it nicely towards mid off for a quick run.

FOUR! Easy pickings! The Indians are feeling the heat of the final. A juicy full toss outside off, Das doesn't miss out as he opens the face of his bat and carves it past backward point for a boundary. Goes past his highest score in ODIs which was 41.
Good length ball well outside off, it has been run down to third man for a single.
Misses out on a full toss! On middle, Hasan loses a bit of balance as he flicks it away towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full length ball, angling in, defended solidly off the front foot.

SIX! Going, going, gone! Liton is taking the attack to the wily leggie. Tossed up on off, Das clears his front leg and slogs it over cow corner to clear the ropes. 16 from the over, great start for Bangladesh.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.

Good running! Tossed up ball, Mehidy clips it against the spin through mid-wicket and calls for two. Takes the rocket arm of Jadeja on and gets back home successfully. 50 comes up for Bangladesh without the fall of a wicket for the first time in this Asia Cup.
Full and straight, driven hard towards Chahal who dives to his right but fails to stop it cleanly. A run is stolen.

SIX! Boom! He reads the wrong one in a jiffy and dismisses it from his presence. Floated on middle and leg, Liton kneels and slog sweeps it over square leg to clear the ropes. First maximum of the innings.
Quicker, flatter and on middle and leg, Liton stays leg side of the ball and dead-bats it.
A full toss on middle and off, Liton misses out as he flicks it off the inner half through square leg for a run.
FOUR! Shot! Talk about confidence and there was a truckload of it. Bumrah spots Das using his feet and he shortens his length. Das pulls it hard over mid-wicket to find the fence.
Bumrah bowls this one in the tight off stump corridor, Liton with his bat close to his pad presents a water-tight defense.
Angling in from a good length, deflected neatly off his pads towards fine leg to rotate strike.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a length outside off, Mehidy taps it with an open bat face towards point.
Turning away from middle and leg, worked against the spin to the leg side for a run. This is now the best opening partnership for Bangladesh against India across all Asia Cups.
On middle and off, Das clears his front leg and heaves it over mid-wicket. Not off the meat and he will only get a single for it.

Ooh... that was close! The flipper from Chahal around off, Mehidy goes for a booming drive but gets a bottom edge that just about kisses the off stump. Goes behind past the keeper and a single is taken.
Gives this one a lot of air, Hasan comes forward and defends it nicely.
Slower through the air, kept out watchfully.
Tossed up ball around off, driven towards the left of Chahal who dives to stop it.
Spin introduced pretty early. Perhaps for the first time in the tournament, the two pacers have failed to dictate terms in Powerplay 1. Yuzvendra Chahal to roll his arm over.
Short of a length ball outside off, punched crisply off the back foot towards cover-point. 8 from this one.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Length ball on the hips, all Das has to do is to get a tickle on it and he does so. No chance for Jadhav at fine leg to cut it off.

FOUR! Hit with authority! Kumar is looking a bit rattled, hasn't found his rhythm yet. Short ball coming at a good height to Das. He swivels across and pulls it in front of square leg to pick up a boundary.
Better from Kumar this time! This one straightens off the seam from middle stump. Das is hurried a little but blocks it towards covers.
Similar line and length, Liton gets behind the line and defends it with a straight bat.
Short of a length ball, angling in, defended solidly off the back foot.

FOUR! Crisp! That will do his confidence a world of good. He is a very capable batsman. In the Under 19 World Cup, he used to bat up the order so he has experience. Back of a length outside off, Mehidy camps back and punches it through covers to find the fence. 12 from the over.
Wide! A bit harsh call that. Good length ball on middle and off, after pitching, the ball swings down late. Mehidy shuffles and tries to flick it but misses. Bumrah has a wry smile about it.
A bit fuller length ball outside off, pushed away with the angle off the front foot towards point.
Bumrah goes wide of the crease and angles in a back of a length ball. Hasan moves inside the line and tucks it to the leg side.
Liton has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short ball, rising on Liton. He stands tall and pulls it in front of square leg for a couple.

FOUR! Not that convincing but he will take it! On a length, angling in, Das runs down the track and drags his heave through mid-wicket to find the fence. This is now Bangladesh's highest opening partnership in this Asia Cup.

A bit of miscommunication but no harm done! Length ball outside off, tapped towards Jadeja at backward point. Liton takes off and stops a bit  but then decides to get going. Ravindra has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Didn't look that dangerous but the replay shows that had that hit, Mehidy was a goner. A reprieve for him.
The fifth straight ball in a row, tucked with ease towards fine leg for a couple. Bhuvi has lost his radar, perhaps trying to swing it too much.
Beaten! Short and wide, Liton goes for a flashy cut but misses. It was a similar shot to the one Mehidy played unsuccessfully. Needs to be careful in the initial stages.
Leg bye! Once again erring on the leg side, Mehidy tries to tuck it across but the ball brushes his thigh pad and rolls towards square leg. The batsmen steal a run.
Too straight for Bhuvi's liking. It is on a length on the hips and Liton helps it to fine leg to rotate strike.
Back of a length ball, angling in appreciably. Das hops and tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Shaping away on a good length, pushed with an open bat face towards point. 5 from Bumrah's first over.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! Edged but safe! Mehidy would have had his heart in his mouth. A length ball on the fifth stump channel, seaming away. Hasan fishes at it away from his body and gets a thick outside edge. Dhawan at first slip dives to his right but the ball lands in front of him and goes past him to the fence. This is only the third boundary for the Bangladesh openers in the tournament in Powerplay 1.
A rush of blood from Mehidy! He needs to keep his composure. Good length ball well outside off, moving away. Hasan slashes at it but misses.
A touch fuller in length, angling in. Mehidy prods ahead and defends it stoutly.
Bumrah steams in and hits the deck hard outside off. Das places it towards gully for a quick single.
Jasprit Bumrah to bowl with the second new ball.
Full length ball around off, a bit of nibble in the air. Mehidy comes forward and defends it nicely. A good start for Bhuvi, 3 from the first over.
In the same channel and on a same length outside off, shaping away after landing. Hasan plants his front foot across and lets it be.

DROPPED! That was a brilliant effort from Karthik though, would have been a stunner had that been taken. A good length ball outside off, Das tries to glide it down to third man but ends up playing it very fine. Dinesh at wide second slip dives full length, gets his fingertips to it but the ball bursts through. A run results.
On a length outside off, a bit of away seam movement. Liton hangs back and plays it with an angled blade towards backward point.
A bit fuller on the fifth stump channel and the ball swings away. Mehidy gets to the pitch of the ball and runs it down towards third man to get off the mark as well.
Starts off with a good length ball outside off, a hint of away shape on that. Das runs it past the wide second slip fielder and gets underway.

The teams are out for their respective national anthems. After the completion, we are all set to go. Liton Das and Mehidy Hasan will open the batting for Bangladesh. Surprise, surprise! Mehidy was the highest scorer for them in the previous game against India and hence, the decision to give him a shot at the top. Two slips in place. Bhuvneshwar Kumar to steam in with the first new ball. Here we go...

The big guns are back for the Men in Blue. Rohit Sharma, Shikhar Dhawan, Yuzvendra Chahal, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Jasprit Bumrah return to the playing XI. KL Rahul, Manish Pandey, Siddarth Kaul, Khaleel Ahmed and Deepak Chahar are the ones who miss out today.

Bangladesh skipper, Mashrafe Mortaza, credits his boys for the way they have performed so far. Adds that today is a big day and they have to give their best. Mentions that Mominul Haque misses out and the left-arm spinner Nazmul Islam comes in so they are going in with five bowlers. States that India are the no. 1 side but if they give it their all, anything can happen.

India skipper, Rohit Sharma, says that they will field first. Adds that they have done that throughout the tournament. Mentions that fielding first suits them and there is no reason to change that. States that they knew it will be a challenging tournament but his boys have responded brilliantly. Adds that this is the last hurdle to cross. Reckons that the first goal was to qualify for the final. Informs that the five guys who missed out in the last game are back.
TOSS - Mashrafe Mortaza calls tails but the coin lands as heads. India win the toss and opt to field.

PITCH REPORT - Ramiz Raza and Sunil Gavaskar are out in the middle assessing the surface. The former says that it looks very good for batting. Gavaskar adds that India will like this pitch. Feels that the ball tends to skid on better in the second half. Mentions there was some turn for the Afghan spinners in the last game here and also for Jadeja. Adds that the track might crumble a bit and it will aid the slow bowlers. States that Bangladesh used Sarkar very well with the ball. Reckons that they have strong desire and that will help them a lot in the final. Ends by saying that the batsmen will more or less enjoy themselves.

In the Asia Cup (ODIs and T20Is), India have a 12-1 win record against Bangladesh. They had won the 2016 T20 final convincingly in Dhaka as well, so that will act as a psychological boost for them. Will the Men in Blue continue their domination or will we see Bangladesh touch the zenith of success today? The Bangla Tigers haven't won the trophy ever and it will drive them further. Expect an edge-of-the-seat encounter.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, have good momentum on their side. Credit to them for reaching this far without their superstars, Tamim Iqbal and Shakib Al Hasan. This is a team which believes in itself and though it took a bashing against India in the previous game, it can be taken lightly only at your own peril. The Bangla top order is a worry for them but today is perhaps the apt occasion for them to come out all guns blazing.

Six teams sweated it out in the grueling heat but two teams have held their own to come out with flying colors - India and Bangladesh. The Men in Blue have fired on all cylinders all through the tournament while it has been the persistence of the Bangla Tigers which has brought them to the finals of the Asia Cup. A tough-fought tie against Afghanistan augurs well for India and the big guns returning to the mix will only boost their confidence further.
